object.title: Uniform-fiber conjecture for quantum lens-space equivalence classes
object.statement: Let $S_{r,n}$ be the parameter set for the quantum lens spaces under consideration, and let $\sim$ be the equivalence relation on it. **Uniform-fiber conjecture.** All equivalence classes of the quotient $S_{r,n}/\sim$ have the same cardinality. The paper presents this as a consequence that would follow from the two preceding conjectures, so it remains open.
object.source_name: Peter Lunding Jensen, Frederik Ravn Klausen and Peter M. R. Rasmussen, “Combinatorial classification of quantum lens spaces”, arXiv:1701.04003 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.04003

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

object.title: Wu–Li's permutation-polynomial conjecture for odd extensions of $5$
object.statement: Let $k$ be a positive odd integer and let $f(x)=x\big(\frac{x^2-x+2}{x^2+x+2}\big)^2$ over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{5^k}$. **Wu–Li's conjecture.** The polynomial $f$ is a permutation polynomial of $\mathbb{F}_{5^k}$. This is one of two conjectures proposed by Wu and Li concerning permutation trinomials over finite fields; the paper states that both conjectures are settled.
object.source_name: Jingxue Ma and Gennian Ge, “A note on permutation polynomials over finite fields”, arXiv:1703.03158 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.03158

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: Ma's Nordhaus–Gaddum conjecture for total-rainbow connection number
object.statement:
Let $G$ and $\overline{G}$ be complementary connected graphs with $n$ vertices. **Ma's conjecture.** There exist constants $C_1$ and $C_2$ such that

$$
trc(G)+trc(\overline{G})\leq C_1n+C_2,
$$

and this upper bound is tight. This asks for a tight linear Nordhaus–Gaddum-type upper bound for total-rainbow connection number; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
object.source_name: Wenjing Li, Xueliang Li, Colton Magnant and Jingshu Zhang, “Tight Nordhaus-Gaddum-type upper bound for total-rainbow connection number of graphs”, arXiv:1703.04065 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.04065

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

object.title: The finite D3-minus-C conjecture for short intervals
object.statement: A finite poset is **D3-minus-C** if it satisfies the D3-minus-C axiom, and it has **Short intervals are Small** when that property holds. **Finite D3-minus-C conjecture.** If a finite poset is D3-minus-C, then it has Short intervals are Small and is vertically transitive. This is presented as the conjectured converse of Part (d) of the preceding theorem; the source does not provide a resolution.

object.title: The TDC-stability conjecture for graphs with a vertex of degree one or two
object.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with a vertex of degree one or two. **TDC-stability conjecture.** Then $St_d^t(G)=1$ or $St_d^t(G)=2$. This conjecture concerns Nordhaus–Gaddum-type questions for the total dominator chromatic stability number; the source presents it as an open problem following a lower bound for $St_d^t(G)+St_d^t(G^c)$, while sharp upper bounds remain open.
object.source_name: Nima Ghanbari and Saeid Alikhani, “More on the total dominator chromatic number of a graph”, arXiv:1705.10231 (2017).

object.title: The semi-cross lattice tiling conjecture
object.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, and define the semi-cross

$$
V_{p-1}=\{\mathbf{0},\mathbf{e}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{e}_{p-1}\}\subset\mathbb{Z}^{p-1}.
$$

**Semi-cross lattice tiling conjecture.** Every tiling of $\mathbb{Z}^{p-1}$ by $V_{p-1}$ is lattice. The paper states that this special case is equivalent to the prime-tile lattice tiling conjecture, via the universal semi-cross construction.

object.title: Jiang, Li and Zhang's total monochromatic connection conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. **Jiang, Li and Zhang's conjecture.** It always holds that

$$
\operatorname{tmc}(G)>\operatorname{mc}(G).
$$

The conjecture compares the total monochromatic connection number with the monochromatic connection number for connected graphs; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

object.title: Terao-type conjecture for the invariant ν of line arrangements
object.statement:
Let $C:f=0$ be a line arrangement in $\mathbb{P}^2$. The invariant $\nu(C)$ is a combinatorial invariant of $C$.

**Terao-type conjecture.** The invariant $\nu(C)$ is combinatorially determined.

This is presented as a stronger version of H. Terao's conjecture that freeness of a line arrangement is combinatorially determined. The source gives no resolution status for this stronger statement.

object.title: The conjecture that the upper bound for beta_2 is sharp
object.statement:
For integers $k$ and $r$ satisfying

$$
2\le r<k<2r-1,
$$

let $\beta_2(k,r)$ be the parameter defined in the paper. **The sharpness conjecture for $\beta_2$.** One has

$$
\beta_2(k,r)=4r-k-2.
$$

This conjecture would make the upper bound in Proposition stated in the paper an equality throughout the indicated range; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

object.title: Symmetry criterion for facet-defining building block classes
object.statement: Let $\mathcal T^{\bm m}$ be a valid building block class for the constructed inequalities. **Symmetry criterion.** The class $\mathcal T^{\bm m}$ is facet-defining if and only if it is symmetric. The paper proves facet-defining results for almost doubly-symmetric valid classes, but this if-and-only-if characterization is presented as a conjecture and remains open.

object.title: Heath–Pemmaraju square-root conjecture for planar posets
object.statement: Let $P$ be a planar poset on $n$ elements, and let ${\operatorname{qn}}(P)$ denote its queue-number. **Heath–Pemmaraju's square-root conjecture.** Every planar poset on $n$ elements has queue-number at most $\lceil \sqrt{n} \rceil$. The paper recalls this as an open problem about bounding the queue-number of planar posets in terms of their number of elements; no resolution is given.

object.title: Conjectured first diagonal formula for $C_{2,t}$
object.statement:
Let $C_{2,t}(n,k)$ be the composition-counting function. **First-diagonal conjecture.** If $t$ is even, then

$$
C_{2,t}(t+s,\tfrac{t}{2}+s)=\tfrac{t}{2}+\tfrac{t}{2}s
$$

for integers $t>2$ and $s\geq 0$. This describes one of the first nonzero diagonals in the even-$t$ case; no proof or resolution is given.
object.source_name: Vincent E. Coll,, Aria Dougherty, Matthew Hyatt, Andrew W. Mayers and Nick W. Mayers, “On compositions associated to seasweed subalgebras of sl(n)”, arXiv:1808.01008 (2018).

object.title: Nonprime partition nonequivalence conjecture for consumption and dominance orderings
object.statement: Let the consumption ordering and dominance ordering be the two orderings on partitions of $n$ introduced in the paper. **The nonprime partition nonequivalence conjecture.** If $n$ is not prime, then the consumption ordering on partitions of $n$ is not equivalent to the dominance ordering. The paper presents this as the dual conjecture to the prime case.
object.source_name: Caleb Ji, “Distinguishing Numbers and Generalizations”, arXiv:1808.01074 (2019).

object.title: Anti-labeling conjecture for two-dimensional grids
object.statement:
Let $G=P_m\times P_n$ be a two-dimensional grid, and let $m=\min\{m,n\}$. **Grid anti-labeling conjecture.** One has

$$
mc^{nh}_{mn}(G)=\left\lfloor\frac{mn-m}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

The paper proves the displayed quantity as a lower bound by explicit labelings. The conjecture is that this lower bound is always sharp for two-dimensional grids.

object.title: The dumbbell graph Tait polynomial characterization conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected planar trivalent graph, and let $T_G(z)$ denote its Tait polynomial. **Dumbbell graph characterization conjecture.** If

$$
T_G(z)=z^{-1}-1+z-z^2,
$$

then $G$ is the dumbbell graph. The source supplies no resolution of this characterization conjecture.
object.source_name: Scott Baldridge, “A Cohomology Theory for Planar Trivalent Graphs with Perfect Matchings”, arXiv:1810.07302 (2023).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.07302

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2018). “This is equivalent to the four color theorem---a famous conjecture in mathematics that was proven with the aid of a computer in the 1970s.”

object.title: The Tait polynomial characterization of four-colorability
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar trivalent graph, and let $T_G$ denote its Tait polynomial. **Tait polynomial four-colorability conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $4$-colorable if and only if

$$
T_G(1)>0.
$$

The source presents this as conditional on positivity properties of the $2$-factor polynomial and gives no resolution independent of those results.

object.title: The complete bipartite rook equivalence graph conjecture for Ferrers boards
object.statement: Let $K_{a,b}$ be a complete bipartite graph, and let $B$ be a Ferrers board whose rook equivalence graph is $K_{a,b}$. **Complete bipartite rook equivalence conjecture.** Then $a=b=1$. This conjecture concerns which graphs can arise as rook equivalence graphs of Ferrers boards; the paper presents it as a future project, and no resolution is supplied here.

object.title: Mazzuoccolo's bipartite-complement conjecture for cubic graphs
object.statement: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. **Mazzuoccolo's conjecture.** There exist two perfect matchings $M_1,M_2$ such that the graph obtained by deleting their union, $G\setminus(M_1\cup M_2)$, is bipartite. The source presents this as a weakening of the preceding perfect-matching conjectures; no resolution is supplied here.
